text:
marta: Heads-up — seeing reproducible memory growth on long-context runs when PagedAttention is enabled on mixed H100/RTX clusters. Looks like page-table coalesce and eviction ordering are fighting each other, leaving stale mappings. Attaching short logs and counters I captured.

marta: log snippet (from debug level):
```
[KVPage] alloc page_id=0x7f2c size=65536 owner_gpu=H100
[KVPage] coalesce_merge_count=3 coalesce_failures=1
[KVPT] insert CAS failed -> fallback_push owner=RTX6000
[KVPage] ghost_entries=12 reclaimed=4
[KVPage] total_pages=384 free_pages=18
```

kevin: :eyes: can you share the exact command/bench? I want to try repro on a pure H100 node as well.

marta: repro command: `./tools/bench_paged_attn --model gpt2-xl --batch 16 --seq 8192 --mixed-gpu h100,rtx`
Also ran with `--kv-debug=page,pt` and produced the snippet above.

jia: this rings a bell — we had a subtle ordering assumption in PT coalesce where we assume owner gpu id monotonicity during merges. On mixed setups PCIe bus ordering+driver timings can reorder completions. CAS fallback path may leave a transient stale owner pointer.

nate: did you see eviction traces? does the pager ever free a page that a different GPU later tries to claim?

marta: yes — eviction logs show page freed on GPU A, then reclaimed by GPU B but PT still had a stale slot pointing to old page_id until next full sync. That gap correlates with the memory bump.

kevin: quick hack: try disabling PT coalescing in runtime (`--kv-coalesce=off`). If memory pressure stabilizes that strongly suggests coalesce/evict race.

marta: tried that — memory growth stops (ran 30m). Perf drop ~6% but stable.

jia: good repro. I suspect the root is a non-atomic sequence: 1) free page, 2) coalesce writes, 3) PT update uses CAS that compares only pointer not version. On reordering across GPUs CAS can succeed incorrectly. Need a version/tag in the PT slot.

nate: +1 on versioned slot. We tried a low-overhead generation counter before but removed it for perf reasons. Maybe reintroduce with 16-bit epoch to avoid wrap concerns.

kevin: also check the kernel selection path — H100 uses async-copy + atomics; RTX kernels use different fence semantics. Might be that the H100 kernel publishes mapping before writes are visible to other devices.

marta: filing issue and attaching repro: https://internal/issue/IR-4321 (repro dir: /eng-runtime/bench/kvcache-repro-196880). Created a tiny repro that toggles coalesce and simulates staggered reclaim.

infra-bot: Deploy note — canary runtime build `redwood/runtime:kvcache-pt-fix` scheduled to eng-runtime-canary tonight 03:00 UTC.

kevin: I'll try to instrument PT writes with memory barriers and add a small sequence number in the slot. If that fixes the race we can optimize later.

marta: thanks — if you need logs from the mixed cluster I left the fuller trace at `/mnt/logs/kvcache/196880/`.

nate: when you push a point-fix PR, add a perf microbenchmark; we need to ensure the added fencing/versioning doesn't regress token throughput too much.

marta: noted. I'll update the issue with measurements after a couple of iterations.

kevin: timeline: try a change this week, run canary next Tue. If all green, push hotfix backport to current stable branch.

marta: cool. tagging @jia @nate for visibility. :thumbsup:
